pointers.sentence: Both ASGI changes came in 6.2 and concern the one thread each request has, on which Django runs the synchronous code it calls with `thread_sensitive=True` (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.__call__`).
The notes give two reasons: the cost of switching to that thread and back for each hook, and the database connections an error view uses (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).
Since 6.2 a chain of Django's own middleware under ASGI is one call into the request's thread (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`).

Each class Django builds on `MiddlewareMixin` with a `process_request` or a `process_response` now sets `async_capable = False`, the flag that says whether a middleware can run on the event loop, where it took the mixin's `True` (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.async_capable`).

At this commit the middleware's are two: the chain, and `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`, still handed over on its own, as the view is (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response_async`).

Listed last, it runs in async mode as before; directly before one of Django's synchronous ones, it now runs synchronously, in their one call (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.async_capable`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`; [Sync and async in one chain](../handlers/async.md)).

Listed last, it runs in async mode as before; directly before one of Django's synchronous ones, it now runs synchronously, in their one call (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.async_capable`, `django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.load_middleware`; [Sync and async in one chain](../handlers/async.md)).
The old import still works, and warns with `RemovedInDjango2029Warning` (`django/utils/deprecation.py:__getattr__`; [What changed](../changes.md#an-old-habit-release-by-release)).
That call now passes `thread_sensitive=True` (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:convert_exception_to_response`; [How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md)).
A connection belongs to the thread that opened it (`django/db/utils.py:ConnectionHandler.thread_critical`).
`close_old_connections`, which closes one broken or past its age, runs on the request's thread as the request starts and ends (`django/db/__init__.py:close_old_connections`).
It guarded against an attack on a JSON array through JavaScript's array prototype, which ECMAScript 5 closed, the 6.2 notes say (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).
The default of `safe=` is now `None`, read as false (`django/http/response.py:JsonResponse.__init__`).
Before 6.1 it decoded such a part leniently: invalid data "could be silently ignored or result in empty values", the 6.1 notes say (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

`MultiPartParser.parse` now decodes with `validate=True`, which refuses any character outside the Base64 alphabet (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.parse`; [Multipart parsing: `MultiPartParser`](../http/multipart.md)).
The handler answers `MultiPartParserError` with a 400 (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).
Since 6.1 a field whose Base64 is written in lines, as MIME writes it, arrives undecoded, while the same data in a file still decodes (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser.parse`).
| a form not in UTF-8 | Since 5.0, a urlencoded body declared in another charset raises `BadRequest`, a 400 | `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files` |
| `HttpRequest.get_preferred_type` | New in 5.2: of the types given, the one the client prefers | `django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.get_preferred_type` |
| `method_decorator` | Since 5.2, marks its replacement a coroutine function when the method is one | `django/utils/decorators.py:_multi_decorate` |
| `RedirectView.preserve_request` | New in 6.1: given to the response the view makes | `django/views/generic/base.py:RedirectView.get` |

| `max_length=` of a redirect | New in 6.1, keyword-only: `MAX_URL_REDIRECT_LENGTH` unless given, `None` for no limit; `redirect` takes it too | `django/http/response.py:HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__` |
| get_converter | Gone in 5.1; the registry is read through `get_converters` | `django/urls/converters.py:get_converters` |
